en: The Sūtra on the Auspicious Signs of the Twelvefold Dependent Origination, Volume One.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Dharma Master and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, under Imperial Decree during the Western Heaven (India). Presented by the Subject Śīladharma.
Thus have I heard:
At one time the World-Honored One was sitting cross-legged in the midst of a great assembly.
Then the entire multitude, surrounding him with reverence and gazing up at the Tathāgata, spoke these verses before the Buddha:
I prostrate to the ocean of the Buddha’s virtues, the true and perfectly enlightened one,
who has expounded the dharma of dependent origination for the past and the future.
The world’s false views cause beings to sink into suffering through their inversions.
"Afflictions and karma are boundless; we pray that the Buddha will proclaim them for us.
At that time, the assembly—consisting of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of humans and devas—addressed the Buddha, saying:
"This great multitude, as well as those of the future, desire to hear the profound Dharma; we only pray that you will expound it."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly:
"Excellent, excellent! You should listen attentively; I shall now speak for your sake."
"O sons of noble family!

If you wish to thoroughly understand the auspicious and auspiciously responsive signs of the twelvefold dependent origination—from ignorance through to old age and death—and their sequential rotation, such that distinct auspicious omens arise in each of the twelve months, listen."

From the first month of winter down to the ninth month, and from the first day of the month up to the fifteenth, he tested for auspicious signs; matters of joy and sorrow, happiness and suffering, were not of a single kind.
“Good sons, these twelve links begin from the month of Puṣya: on the first day is ignorance; on the second day, old age and death;

on the third day, the link of birth; on the fourth day, the link of existence; on the fifth day, the link of grasping; on the sixth day, the link of craving; on the seventh day, the link of sensation; on the eighth day, the link of contact; on the ninth day, the six sense bases; on the tenth day, name-and-form; on the eleventh day, the link of consciousness; and on the twelfth day, the link of volitional formations.”
Furthermore, from the eleventh month, Makhā: on the first day is *saṅkhāra*; on the second day, *avijjā*;

on the third day, *jarāmaraṇa*; on the fourth day, *jāti*; on the fifth day, *bhava*; on the sixth day, *upādāna*; on the seventh day, *taṇhā*; on the eighth day, *vedanā*; on the ninth day, *phassa*; on the tenth day, *saḷāyatana*; on the eleventh day, *nāmarūpa*; and on the twelfth day, *viññāṇa*.
Furthermore, from the twelfth month, *Parāṇa-māsa*, [the twelve links are assigned as follows]:

the first day is consciousness (*vijñāna*), the second day is formations (*saṃskāra*), the third day is ignorance (*avidyā*), the fourth day is aging and death (*jarāmaraṇa*), the fifth day is birth (*jāti*), the sixth day is becoming (*bhava*), the seventh day is grasping (*upādāna*), the eighth day is craving (*tṛṣṇā*), the ninth day is sensation (*vedanā*), the tenth day is contact (*sparśa*), the eleventh day is the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), and the twelfth day is name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*).
Furthermore, from the month of Caitra: on the first day is name-and-form; on the second day, consciousness;

on the third day, formations; on the fourth day, ignorance; on the fifth day, aging-and-death; on the sixth day, birth; on the seventh day, existence; on the eighth day, grasping; on the ninth day, craving; on the tenth day, sensation; on the eleventh day, contact; and on the twelfth day, the six sense bases.
Furthermore, from Vaiśākha: on the first day, the six sense bases;

on the second day, name-and-form; on the third day, the factor of consciousness; on the fourth day, the factor of volitional formations; on the fifth day, ignorance; on the sixth day, aging and death; on the seventh day, birth; on the eighth day, becoming; on the ninth day, grasping; on the tenth day, craving; on the eleventh day, sensation; and on the twelfth day, contact.
Furthermore, from the *ṛtusaṃjñā*: the first day is the limb of contact (*sparśa*); the second day, the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*);

the third day, name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*); the fourth day, consciousness (*vijñāna*); the fifth day, formations (*saṃskāra*); the sixth day, ignorance (*avidyā*); the seventh day, aging and death (*jarāmaraṇa*); the eighth day, birth (*jāti*); the ninth day, becoming (*bhava*); the tenth day, grasping (*upādāna*); the eleventh day, craving (*tṛṣṇā*); and the twelfth day, sensation (*vedanā*).
Furthermore, from Āśāḍha to Kārttika: the first day is the limb of sensation (vedanā);

the second day is the limb of contact (sparśa); the third day is the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana); the fourth day is name-and-form (nāmarūpa); the fifth day is consciousness (vijñāna); the sixth day is formations (saṃskāra); the seventh day is ignorance (avidyā); the eighth day is old age and death (jarāmaraṇa); the ninth day is birth (jāti); the tenth day is becoming (bhava); the eleventh day is grasping (upādāna); and the twelfth day is craving (tṛṣṇā).
Furthermore, from the month of Śrāvaṇa: on the first day is the limb of Desire (tṛṣṇā);

on the second day, the limb of Grasping (upādāna); on the third day, the limb of Contact (sparśa); on the fourth day, the limb of the Six Sense Bases (ṣaḍāyatana); on the fifth day, the limb of Name-and-Form (nāmarūpa); on the sixth day, the limb of Consciousness (vijñāna); on the seventh day, the limb of Volitional Formations (saṃskāra); on the eighth day, Ignorance (avidyā); on the ninth day, Aging-and-Death (jarāmaraṇa); on the tenth day, the limb of Birth (jāti); on the eleventh day, the limb of Existence (bhava); and on the twelfth day, the limb of Grasping (upādāna).
Furthermore, from the month of Vāruṇa-bhādrapada: on the first day is the limb of Grasping (upādāna); on the second day, Affection (tṛṣṇā);

on the third day, Appropriation (vedanā); on the fourth day, Contact (sparśa); on the fifth day, the Six Sense Bases (ṣaḍāyatana); on the sixth day, Name-and-Form (nāmarūpa); on the seventh day, the limb of Consciousness (vijñāna); on the eighth day, Volitional Formations (saṃskāra); on the ninth day, Ignorance (avidyā); on the tenth day, Old Age and Death (jarāmaraṇa); on the eleventh day, the limb of Birth (jāti); and on the twelfth day, the limb of Existence (bhava).
Furthermore, from the month of Āṣāḍha: on the first day is the limb of *vijñapti* (perception);

on the second day, *ādāna* (appropriation); on the third day, *tṛṣṇā* (craving); on the fourth day, *vedanā* (feeling); on the fifth day, *sparśa* (contact); on the sixth day, the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*); on the seventh day, name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*); on the eighth day, the limb of consciousness (*vijñāna*); on the ninth day, the limb of formations (*saṃskāra*); on the tenth day, ignorance (*avidyā*); on the eleventh day, aging-and-death (*jarāmaraṇa*); and on the twelfth day, the limb of birth (*jāti*).
Furthermore, from the month of Kārttika: on the first day is the limb of birth; on the second day, the limb of existence;

on the third day, the limb of grasping; on the fourth day, the limb of craving; on the fifth day, the limb of sensation; on the sixth day, the limb of contact; on the seventh day, the six sense bases; on the eighth day, name-and-form; on the ninth day, the limb of consciousness; on the tenth day, the limb of formations; on the eleventh day, ignorance; and on the twelfth day, aging and death.
Furthermore, from the month of Mārgaśīrṣa: on the first day is old age and death; on the second day, the link of birth; on the third day, the link of existence;

on the fourth day, the link of grasping; on the fifth day, the link of craving; on the sixth day, the link of sensation; on the seventh day, the link of contact; on the eighth day, the six sense bases; on the ninth day, name-and-form; on the tenth day, the link of consciousness; on the eleventh day, the link of volitional formations; and on the twelfth day, ignorance.
"The thirteenth day of each month is treated like the third;
the fourteenth day is the same as the fourth;
and the fifteenth day, the fifth, follows this same principle."
The commentary states:

"The links of dependent origination follow the forward order; accumulating days, they flow against the current for the remainder of the bright and dark fortnights, as explained at length in the sūtra.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly:
"If there is another person who carefully examines the twelve links [of dependent origination], remembers them without forgetting, and understands their joys and sorrows:
if one is born on a day corresponding to the link of ignorance (*avidyā*), there will be difficulties on the ninth day, in the ninth month, and in the ninth year."

If his life-span is not exhausted, he will possess happiness and wealth, yet his kinsmen will be discordant; he will be free from illness but talkative, live for eighty-one years, and pass away on a day of travel.
"If a child is born on a *caraṇa*-day, there will be danger on the eighth day, the eighth month, or the eighth year.

Unless they die, they will attain great wealth and status; they will have only one brother, live long with little illness, possess virtuous conduct and knowledge of the Dharma, have many friends, and be skilled in arts and crafts. Their lifespan will be eighty-eight years, and they will pass away on a *vijñāna*-day."
“On the day the consciousness enters the womb, on the fifth day, month, and year, there will be an obstacle.

Unless he meets his end, he will be hunchbacked yet courageous; he will constantly lack wealth and treasures, but those who see him will rejoice. His lifespan will be sixty-four years, at which point he will pass away from name-and-form.”
"Name-and-form will arise on the sixth day of the month; in the ninth or tenth year, one will encounter difficult circumstances.

Unless life comes to an end, there will be little illness but many grievances; one's children will have short lifespans; there will be fear of poverty, followed by wealth and honor; one will delight in giving alms and live to eighty years of age, finally passing away through the six sense bases."
Born on the day of the sixth sense-base (ṣaḍāyatana), one encounters calamities on the fifth day, within the third or fourth month, or at the ages of eight or ten.

Unless their lifespan is exhausted, such a person will be prone to envy, suffer from many illnesses, be impoverished yet fierce, crave flavors with stingy greed, live for sixty-four years, and pass away on a Touch-day (sparśa).
"Born on a *sparśa* day, there will be difficulties in the second and fifth years, within the third and ninth months, and during the ninth year.

Unless he meets his end prematurely, he will suffer from chronic illness; he will be eloquent and knowledgeable in the Dharma, yet prone to thievery, lewdness, and the view of self-existence (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*). Possessing wealth, he will be envious of others' beauty. His lifespan will be sixty-four years, and he will pass away on a *sparśa* day."
"One born on the second day of the month will face difficulties in the second, eighth, or eighth year.

Unless they die prematurely, they will always dwell in a position of honor, possess great wealth and noble virtue, have two wives and much property, be skilled in arts and crafts, live for sixty years, and pass away during a period of affection."
"One born under the constellation Ai Ri will experience difficulties on the tenth day, in the third and fifth months, and at nine years of age.

Unless their life-span is exhausted, they will be foremost among the wealthy and noble, have many descendants, suffer little illness but many grievances, live for sixty-four years, and pass away under the constellation Qu."
"Born on the day of *Taka* (the 19th lunar mansion), within the ninth decade of life, there will be difficulties during the second, eighth, and ninth months, and in the ninth year.

Unless his life-span is exhausted, he will face the difficulty of being treated with contempt; his friends will become violent and evil, he will accumulate many enemies, commit wrongful acts, and violate the precepts. His lifespan will be sixty-four years, and he shall pass away on a day."
"Born on a Sunday, reaching the ninth day, in the second or eighth month, or at nine years of age, there will be danger.

Unless his life is exhausted, he will covet the wives and daughters of others, sleep little, belong to a noble clan, serve as a commander of troops, and live for sixty years, passing away on the day of his birth-sign."
"The child will raise offspring; on the fifth day, there will be danger in the ninth month, the ninth year, and the tenth year.

Unless his life-span is exhausted, he will be wealthy and noble yet frequently ill; he will protect the state and honor virtue, live to the age of seventy, and pass away from old age on a day of death."
"Old age and death arise on the day of birth. On the second day, within the ninth month, there will be difficulties for nine years.

Unless his lifespan is exhausted, he will be deluded by folly, beset by thieves of greed and anger, possess an intelligent and sharp nature, have harmonious kinsmen, and many enemies. His lifespan will be sixty-four [years], and he will conclude his life through the link of ignorance (*avidyā*). The foregoing concludes the examination of auspicious signs."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly:
"If there is anyone who falls ill on the day after tomorrow, it shall be a calamity caused by yakṣas; one should maintain diligent protection, and they will recover on the fifth night."
"If one falls ill on a *xing* day, there will be danger on the third or seventh day, but recovery will occur during the second night.
If one falls ill on a *shi* day, there is danger on the fifth day, but recovery will occur during the seventh night."
"If one falls ill on the day of Name-and-Form (nāmarūpa), there will be danger on the third or fifth day; at that very night, life and death are uncertain.
If one falls ill on the day of the Six Sense Bases (ṣaḍāyatana), there will be danger on the third or fourth day, and recovery occurs on the tenth night."
"If one falls ill on the day of *sparśa*, it will be difficult on the third day; the illness will arise on the eighth day and persist for the duration of a long life.
If one falls ill on the day of *vedanā*, it will be difficult on the fifth day; the illness will arise on the ninth day and last for ten months."
"If one falls ill on the day of *Ai* (Love), there will be danger on the eighth or tenth day; on the nineteenth day, life and death are uncertain.
"If one contracts a disease on the day of *Qu* (Taking), there will be danger on that very day, and one will pass away on the tenth day."
"If one falls ill on a Sunday, there will be danger on the third and ninth days; the illness will persist and not be cured.
If one falls ill on a Thursday (Jīvavāra), there will be danger on the fifth day; the illness will arise on the eighth day and, though there is danger until the twelfth day, it will be cured."
"The affliction of the branch of old age and death will reach its critical point on the third day; if there is danger, it shall arise and then be cured.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly, saying:
"Furthermore, if there is a person who, when setting out on a journey, contemplates the twelve links [of dependent origination], they should know whether it is auspicious or inauspicious."

If you travel east tomorrow, you will go to a place of peace, happiness, and well-being and return quickly; if you travel south, you will encounter disputes but obtain what you seek; when traveling west, you will hear things that are disagreeable; and in the north, you will hear sounds that are harmonious, beautiful, and pleasing.

"When the day of the Saṃskāra division arises: if one travels east, one will return safely and without obstruction; if one travels south, one will return from distress with peace and happiness; if one travels west, one will obtain abundant food and drink on the road; if one travels north, one will return safely and in peace."

"If consciousness travels eastward, the journey will be arduous; traveling south, one shall return to one's original place; traveling west, there will be disputes and what is gained will be wasted; traveling north, one shall obtain profit and return to one's original place."

"If Name-and-Form travels eastward, there will be auspiciousness and prosperity; when traveling south, all matters will be fulfilled; when traveling west, all requests will be granted; and when departing northward, the journey will be fraught with hardship."

"If one travels east from the six sense bases, one will obtain wealth and profit; traveling south brings auspiciousness, and one's intentions will be fulfilled upon returning; when traveling west, all wishes will be complete and everything will be accomplished; and when traveling north, whatever is sought shall be attained."

"If the Sun touches [the asterism] and travels eastward, wealth and goods will be lost; traveling south brings peace and happiness; when traveling westward, there will be disputes and alarm; if it quickly turns northward, wealth and profit will increase."

"When the sun moves eastward, one suffers from distress, anxiety, and fear; though these may be avoided in the past, when it moves southward, there will be alarm, fear, and litigation. When it moves westward, one suddenly hears news of a death; when it moves northward, one gains profit and fulfills one's intentions, yet hearing such news brings no joy."

"When the Sun travels on the day of the branch of Love (Mṛgaśirā): traveling eastward, one obtains wealth; traveling south, there is benefit for women; returning quickly to one's original place; when traveling westward, people suddenly gain trust; and traveling north, one’s wishes are fulfilled with sovereign happiness."

"When the sun moves, if it travels eastward, there will be alarm and fear, and the journey will be arduous and painful; if it travels southward, there will be peace and happiness; when it travels westward, there will be slight apprehension; and when it travels northward, all that is sought shall be obtained—therefore, quickly return to its original place."

"If one travels east during the *bhava-aṅga*, there will be hardship and fear; if one travels south, one will quickly reach one's destination, gaining profit and fulfilling one's intentions; if one travels west, all matters will flourish and one will quickly reach one's destination; if one travels north, one will gain benefit and quickly return to one's original place."

"If one travels east during the birth-branch, one will gain wealth but suffer ruin; traveling south brings fulfillment of one's desires; when traveling west, one reaches one's original destination; and traveling north, one acquires wealth."

"Old age and death travel eastward, yet they quickly turn back; when traveling south, one hears words of endearment; traveling west brings fear and dread; when traveling north, one returns safely and in peace to one's original place, having completed the journey."
At that time, the great assembly again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“In this world there are thieves; how can one come to know them clearly?
Thereupon, the World-Honored One told the great assembly:
"If you wish to understand matters such as robbery and theft, you should carefully examine the twelve links of existence (*dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda*).
O sons of good family!

If there is no moon, and a thief comes from the north, your wealth will be scattered; if a thief enters from the east of the house with a malicious intent, that thief has short hair and his dwelling place is not far away; within nine days, you will certainly recover your property."

"If one commits theft on a day governed by the *saṃskāra-aṅga*, their appearance will be reddish-yellow and they will wear old clothes; such a thief incurs punishment, yet if they come from the east, they shall exonerate themselves of the matter."
"If it is the *vijñāna* link, the thief will leave the house with yellowish-red hair and a youthful appearance; when outsiders speak of him and people hear it, the wealth and goods will be recovered.

On the day of the *nāmarūpa* link, there will be two brothers, thieves with black faces and black hair; one among them is ugly and has white hair but is skillful in craft; by the twenty-first [day], the treasures and wealth will be recovered."

"On the sixth day, a thief will emerge from one's own house; he is yellowish-red in appearance, malicious and envious, with large eyes. He will come by way of a watercourse and hide [the goods] near his dwelling place among his kinsmen. On the second day, there will be doubt as to whether they were lost or found, and the matter of the property will remain unsettled."

On the day of the contact factor (sparśa), one commits theft; [the thief] emerges from his own house, tall in stature with black hair, frequently coming with joy, yet always appearing as if weeping due to delusion. If there is a dispute, he shall recover his wealth and goods.

"If one commits theft on the day of the *vedanā* link, the thief will come from within a village; there is a person inside [the house], and the family dog is black in color. By the twentieth day, the thief will certainly be apprehended."

"If one steals on the day of the *Anurādhā* lunar mansion, that person will come from the west and reside in a separate village; he will appear tall and pleasant to behold, his household dog’s paws will be black, and he will be involved in disputes with others. When discussing that person, it will be certain that he is not lying; he will be caught on the day of the *Jyeṣṭhā* lunar mansion."

“If the theft occurs on the day of the *upādāna* link, it comes from the south; there will be a dispute among those within, and through their discussion of the matter, the wealth will certainly be recovered.
If the theft occurs on the day of the *bhava* link, it comes from the east; the culprit is eloquent and boastful, deceitful and highly suspicious, and he speaks of his own kinsmen.”

"If one commits theft on a day ruled by the Jīvapada, three people will travel together: two will come from outside and one will be a close relative. If one seeks it out with great haste, the wealth and treasures will be recovered."

"The thief of the branch of old age and death comes from the north; his body and head are both tall, his teeth are missing, and his hair is white. On the twenty-fifth day, he will recover his wealth and goods; thus ends the discourse on the thief."
At that time, the assembled multitude addressed the Buddha together, saying:
“Regarding the twitching of the limbs, what does it signify?
The Buddha told the great assembly:

"If there should be another person who wishes to know this matter, they ought to examine the twelve links of dependent origination with careful scrutiny and understand that all future sorrows and joys are certainly not false."
"Furthermore, if for men or women the left eye twitches during the phase of Ignorance (*avidyā*), their parents will be struck with fear.
If the left eye twitches during the phase of Volitional Formations (*saṃskāra*), there will be joy and their wishes will be fulfilled."
"If the *vijñāna* branch twitches on the left, the matters sought will be harmonized and accord with one's wishes.
If the *nāmarūpa* branch twitches in the left eye, one will obtain wealth and goods."
"On the day of the *ṣaḍāyatana* limb, if the left eye twitches, one's parents will be displeased.
If it twitches on the day of the *sparśa* limb, there will certainly be disputes.
If it twitches on the day of the *vedanā* limb, one’s sought-after matters will be harmoniously fulfilled."
"If, on a day ruled by the *iṣṭā* nakṣatra, the left eye twitches, one will obtain bone and flesh.
If, on a day ruled by the *grahaṇī* nakṣatra, the left eye twitches, all that is sought shall be obtained."
"If the *bhava-aṅga* (existence) twitches on the left eye, a matter of dispute will arise.
"If the *jāti-aṅga* (birth) twitches in the left eye, one will receive distant news and correspondence.
"Regarding the *jarāmaraṇa-aṅga* (old age and death), when the left eye twitches, all that is sought will be fulfilled as desired."
"If there is another person who observes the twelve links and understands them all completely:
if the right eye twitches regarding the link of ignorance, the parents will be struck with fear."
"When the right eye twitches on the day of the *saṃskāra* link, one will achieve all undertakings according to one's wishes.
When the right eye twitches on the day of the *vijñāna* link, there will be matters involving disputes."
"When the right eye twitches during the phase of name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), one will obtain new clothing.
On the day of the phase of the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), when the right eye twitches, wealth and goods will be dissipated."
"If the right eye twitches on the day of the *sparśa* link, one will obtain wealth and goods.
If it twitches on the day of the *vedanā* link, there will be matters of weeping.
If it twitches on the day of the *tṛṣṇā* link, wealth and goods will be slightly dispersed."
"If the right eye twitches on the day of the *upādāna* link, one will obtain many precious treasures.
If it twitches on the day of the *bhava* link, one will lose wealth in disputes, though it may later be recovered."
"If the twitching of the right eye occurs on the day of the Birth-link (jāti-anga), when one anticipates the arrival of someone or seeks wealth, it is certain that they will come.
On the day of Old Age and Death (jarā-maraṇa-anga), when the right eye twitches, there will be matters of joy and celebration, which will be accomplished through harmony."
The closing of the eyes has been completed.
*The Scripture on the Auspicious Signs of Dependent Origination*, Volume Upper.
*The Scripture on the Auspicious Signs of Dependent Origination*, Volume Lower.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīladharma,
Dharma-transmitting Great Master and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, Subject Shi Hu, under Imperial Decree.
Commentary states:
"The links of existence turn forward, while the days accumulate as they flow backward; the remainder of the dark and light fortnights is as explained at length in the Sūtra.
At that time, an immeasurable assembly of humans and devas addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"The warbling of crows and birds occurs at uncertain times; how can this be known?"
"I pray that the Buddha will expound upon this.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly:
"If there is anyone who carefully and thoroughly observes the twelve links [of dependent origination], they will clearly understand sorrow and joy."
If, on the day of the *avidyā* link, a crow caws to the right, one's wife and daughters will see joy;
if it caws to the left, a traveler will surely arrive.
On the day of the *saṃskāra* link, a caw to the right brings peace and security, while a caw to the left results in the acquisition of wealth.
"On the day of the consciousness link (vijñāna-anga), if it cries to the right, one's aspirations will surely be fulfilled;
if it cries to the left, all aspirations will not be accomplished.
On the day of the name-and-form link (nāmarūpa-anga), crying to the right brings wealth; crying to the left leads to imprisonment."
"Regarding the branch of the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), if it caws on the right, there will be alarm and fear; if it caws on the left, there will be disputes and litigation.
Regarding the day of the branch of contact (*sparśa*), if it caws on the right, there will be alarm and fear; if it caws on the left, family members will arrive."
"On the day of the Vedanā-anga, if the drum sounds on the right, one's wishes are fulfilled;
if it sounds on the left, one gains faith but loses wealth.
On the day of the Tṛṣṇā-anga, if it sounds on the right, there is peace and happiness; if on the left, one obtains virtuous faith."
"On the day of the *upādāna* link, a cry to the right portends suffering and bitterness, while one to the left brings peace and auspiciousness.
On the day of the *bhava* link, a cry to the right indicates being questioned by others, while a cry to the left brings peace and auspiciousness."
"On the day of the birth-linking (*jāti-aṅga*), if it caws to the right, one's sought-after goals will be harmonized and fulfilled;
if it caws to the left, one will gain news, but wealth and property will be dispersed.
On the day of old age and death (*jarāmaraṇa-aṅga*), if it caws to the right, there will be no affliction."
"If it caws on the left, there will be destruction and a small amount of wealth.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the assembled multitude, saying:
"Furthermore, if someone hears a crow cawing in the north regarding the factor of ignorance, they will certainly receive a letter from a visitor."
"On the day of the saṃskāra-link, if a crow caws in the north, there will be joyful news and gains.
On the day of the vijñāna-link, cawing in the north brings peace and security; all will be harmonious and one's wishes fulfilled."
"Regarding the link of name-and-form (nāmarūpa), when the northern direction sounds, one hears pleasant matters.

Regarding the link of the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), if a crow caws in the north, one encounters matters concerning distant travel; wealth and treasures will depart far away, and there will certainly be no harmony."
"If a crow caws in the north on the day of the *sparśa* (contact) link, disputes and litigation will arise.
If it caws in the north on the day of the *vedanā* (feeling) link, there will be peace and security in the north.
If it caws in the north on the day of the *tṛṣṇā* (craving) link, one will be freed from bondage."
"If it cries in the north during the *Jie* (Taking) branch, the undertaking will conclude with the acquisition of trust.
If it cries in the north during the *You* (Existence) branch, clothing and goods will certainly be obtained.
If it cries in the north during the *Sheng* (Birth) branch, someone will come to inquire about matters."
"Old age and death cry out from the north; all is auspicious and secure.
At that time, the great assembly addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"When the upper palate of the heart twitches, how is this to be understood?"
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly, saying:
"If there is anyone who, regarding the twelve links [of dependent origination], recollects them without forgetting and fully comprehends them all."
If the branch of ignorance (*avidyā*) twitches above the palate, a Great Sage will arrive.
If it twitches on the day of the branch of formations (*saṃskāra*), the head of the household will be peaceful and harmonious.
If the branch of consciousness (*vijñāna*) twitches at the palate, a Sage will certainly come.
"If the *nāmarūpa* branch twitches, one will obtain much wealth.
"If the *ṣaḍāyatana* branch twitches, afflictions will arise in the mind.
"If the *sparśa* branch twitches, one will experience pleasant satisfaction and joy."
"If there is a twitching on the day of the *vedanā* link, there will be matters of alarm and fear.
"If there is a twitching on the day of the *tṛṣṇā* link, family wealth will increase.
"If there is a twitching on the day of the *upādāna* link, one person among those present will die prematurely."
"If the *bhava-aṅga* twitches, a noble person will arrive.
"If the *jāti-aṅga* twitches, thieves will certainly come.
"If the *jarāmaraṇa-aṅga* twitches, there will be harmony within the household."
"Furthermore, if there is a person who contemplates the twelve links [of dependent origination] and thoroughly understands sorrow and joy:
when the heart flickers and moves during the link of ignorance (*avidyā*), there will be the afflictions of contention and litigation."
"If the twitching occurs on the day of the *saṃskāra* link, one will obtain wealth and goods.
"If the heart twitches on the day of the *vijñāna* link, there will be matters of alarm and fear.
"If the heart twitches on the day of the *nāmarūpa* link, one's parents will rejoice."
"If the *ṣaḍāyatana* (six sense bases) branch twitches, the matters sought will come together and manifest.
"If the *sparśa* (contact) branch of the mind twitches, one's parents will be struck with fear.
"If the *vedanā* (feeling) branch of the mind twitches, one must travel south to perform an expiation; only then will it be auspicious."
"If the heart throbs during the *tṛṣṇā* (craving) link, one will encounter great distress.
"If it throbs during the *upādāna* (clinging) link, a wicked person will arrive.
"If it throbs during the *bhava* (existence) link, there will be matters of sorrow and grief."
“If the heart-twitch occurs on the day of the birth-link (*jāti-aṅga*), there will surely be great terror.
‘If the heart-twitch and movement occur on the day of the aging-and-death-link (*jarāmaraṇa-aṅga*), the elderly will surely pass away.
At that time, the great assembly again addressed the Buddha, saying:”
"These twelve links possess such auspicious signs; yet regarding the affairs of daily life, we are unable to fully comprehend them. How, then, should we act? We pray that you will explain this."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly, saying:

"Furthermore, if there is anyone who, on the day of the link of ignorance (avidyā) or the link of volitional formations (saṃskāra), holds a banquet, repairs fields or houses, consults on affairs, visits dignitaries, or washes their head—these are auspicious;
however, for bathing or making new clothes, one should not employ these days."

"On the day of the *saṃskāra* link, seeking worldly affairs, listening to the Dharma, practicing archery, subduing enemies and bandits, and bathing before one's elders or superiors are all appropriate and should be well-employed;
however, washing one's head will lead to illness, and making clothes will result in failure—be careful not to do these things."

"On the day of the consciousness link (vijñāna-anga), it is auspicious for a king to receive consecration, to subdue enemies and withdraw his army, to establish villages, prefectures, and dwellings, and all such accomplishments will be successful; it is also suitable for washing the hair, gargling, or anointing the neck, as well as for making clothing.
However, one must exercise extreme caution regarding bathing when feeling startled or terrified."

"If the branch of name-and-form (nāmarūpa) is employed for various tasks, for matters requiring constant attention, for shaving the hair and nails, or for the storage of wealth and goods, it will serve them well;
yet when used for washing the head, its color changes, and when used for bathing, it causes alarm; furthermore, when used to make clothing, it yields joy but quickly tears."

On the day of the *ṣaḍāyatana* (six sense bases) branch: the king receives consecration; villages are established and brought to completion; one should not pay homage to others; moving into a new residence brings loss of wealth; guarding property incurs guilt;
if bathing at this time, one’s parents will be terrified; if washing the head, one’s reputation will be free from fear.
"On the day of the *sparśa* (Contact) factor, performing virtuous deeds will not succeed; evil acts will harm others, and criminal offenses will be swiftly accomplished.

On the day of the *upādāna* (Grasping) factor, whatever one undertakes will cause alarm and fear to one's parents; bathing, making clothes, or being with loved ones will not last long, and there will certainly be blood-related calamities. If one has made clothes but has not yet bathed, one should not wear them."
On the day of the Vedanā-limb (Feeling), matters sought will be met with joy; it is auspicious for trade, giving, the repair of monasteries, and festive celebrations.
Washing the head brings fear; one's desires will not be fulfilled. However, when making robes, what is hoped for will not be difficult to attain; it is auspicious to wear them before friends.
"On the day of the limb of craving (tṛṣṇā), it is auspicious to collect and protect provisions and precious gems;
undertaking minor or urgent tasks brings great anxiety; washing the hair results in failure; and making clothes will be fulfilled."
"On the day of the *upādāna* link, it is appropriate for shaving the hair of a child, performing minor tasks, and all such light activities;

as well as for a teacher initiating a disciple, shaving the beard and hair, compounding medicines, seeing off guests, weddings, auspicious celebrations, attaining wealth, bathing, making clothes, and encountering joy."

"On the day of the *bhava-aṅga*, one should form friendships and acquaintances; all undertakings and legal disputes should be avoided. One must not wash one's head, but making clothes and bathing are both auspicious and favorable."
"On the day of the Jāti branch, it is auspicious for all matters such as repairing houses, saddles, horses, and storehouses, or meeting high-ranking officials and lords;
bathing, traveling afar, and washing the head are likewise appropriate. As for making clothes, it is not for long-term use, but rather one should wear them on that very day."

On the day of the *jarāmaraṇāṅga* (the link of old age and death): whatever evil matters arise, the wealth of the rich shall be dissipated; one will accomplish beneficial deeds and engage in philosophical discourse; one remains far removed from all that is improper; washing the head brings swift results; food and drink are mostly delicious; bathing causes mental distress; and making clothes takes a long time.
Thereupon, the assembly addressed the World-Honored One, saying:

“The twitching of the feet, the shaking of the earth, the cawing of crows and the barking of dogs, the oil lamp and the injury by a rat—since the good and evil [of these omens] have not yet been clarified, we pray that you will explain them for us.”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly, saying:
"If there is anyone who, regarding the twelve links [of dependent origination], practices mindfulness and critical examination, they shall come to know good and evil."
Why is this so? On the day of the link of ignorance (*avidyā*), if the foot twitches, there is cause for joy.
On the day of the link of volitional formations (*saṃskāra*), if the foot twitches, it presages misfortune regarding one's affairs; do not engage in them.
"Regarding the link of consciousness and name-and-form, there is dispute on this day.
On the day of the link of the six sense bases, if one's foot twitches, a person will die.
Regarding the links of contact, feeling, and craving—if these three twitch, matters of dispute will arise."
"On the day of the link of Grasping (*upādāna*), if the foot twitches, a person will die.
On the day of the link of Existence (*bhava*), if the foot twitches, one will obtain clothing.
If the foot twitches on the day of the link of Birth (*jāti*), there will be fear of thieves, calamities, and illness."
"On the day of the link of old age and death (*jarāmaraṇāṅga*), if the foot twitches, one will encounter sorrowful matters.
Furthermore, observing the twelve links of existence (*dvādaśāṅgapratītyasamutpāda*): on the day of the link of ignorance (*avidyāṅga*), when the foot twitches or moves, a robber will arrive;
when a house dog barks, someone will come from afar to inquire."
If the robe is burned, there will be no misfortune;
if the robe is gnawed by mice, danger will arrive;
if a crow caws, a family member will come to inquire.
When clothing is stained by oil, one will suddenly gain the trust of others;
when the earth trembles, the King’s favor descends universally.
On days governed by the *caraṇa-karaṇa*, it is auspicious to go abroad when the feet twitch or move.
If a dog barks, there will be some minor affairs of state;
if a crow caws, a virtuous messenger will surely arrive;
and upon seeing the light of blood or obtaining a burnt garment, one shall find joy.
If mice gnaw the clothes, one will attain great wealth and nobility;
if the clothes are stained with oil, one will acquire much property;
if there is an earthquake, there will be famine, slaughter, and invasion by foreign nations.
"On the day of the consciousness link (vijñāna-anga), when the feet twitch or move, non-human beings arrive;
when dogs bark, thieves and robbers arrive and one acquires wealth;
when crows caw, matters of litigation and dispute arise."
If one's robes are burned, something may be gained;
if the robes are gnawed by mice, wealth lost may be recovered;
and when the robes are stained with oil, one's parents will be struck with alarm.
When there is an earthquake, two kings will engage in annexation.
On the day of the *nāmarūpa* limb, if one's foot twitches, one will obtain wealth that arrives unbidden;
if a dog barks, a person will suddenly die.
If a crow caws or sings, a loved one will arrive;
if a mouse gnaws clothing at an inopportune time, wealth will be lost;
if clothing is scorched, there will be joy.
If one's robes are stained with oil, it portends that a person of high status will think of one;
when there is an earthquake, or when enemies and bandits arise, if one shaves the head, the kingdom will become peaceful.
"On the day of the branch of the six sense bases (ṣaḍāyatana), if the foot twitches, a friend will arrive from afar, and the head of the household will be safe and well."
If a dog barks, there will be strife and litigation;
if a crow caws, a person will arrive to perform matters of reconciliation;
if a rat damages clothing, someone will drown and perish.
If the robe is scorched or damaged, one will obtain wealth through litigation;
if the robe is stained with oil, there will be matters of alarm and fear;
when an earthquake occurs, an elder will pass away.
"On the day of the sparśa-limb, if the foot twitches, one will hear pleasant news;
if a domestic dog barks, thieves will arrive;
if a crow caws, there will be alarm."
When the robe is damaged by mice, one will obtain wealth and goods;
when the robe is scorched by fire, it indicates the death of a person;
when the robe is stained by oil, one will receive joy from one's kinsmen.
The Discourse on Earthquakes and Controversies:
"If, during the day of the *vedanā* branch, the feet twitch or move, it is auspicious to go abroad;
if a domestic dog barks, a noble person (*ārya*) will arrive."
When clothing is damaged by mice, one will certainly encounter its owner;
when damaged by fire, some minor affairs will arise;
when stained by oil, one will experience what is disagreeable.
When an earthquake occurs, distant news will certainly arrive.
On the day of the Āśleṣā nakṣatra, if the foot twitches, one will obtain wealth;
if a dog barks at an improper time, there will surely be anger and litigation.
If a crow caws or sings, one will hear news that brings you joy;
when a rat gnaws your clothes, someone will surely die;
when fire damages your clothes, you will obtain wealth and goods.
When one's robes are stained with oil, there will be auspicious and celebratory matters;
when there is an earthquake, enemies and bandits will surely arise, and a messenger will arrive from the east.
"On the day of the *upādāna* link, if the foot twitches, one incurs misfortune; if a person suddenly gains faith;
if a dog barks at an improper time, there will be litigation;
and when a crow caws, there will be the sudden death of a kinsman."
When clothing is damaged by mice, a famine will arrive;
when clothing is damaged by fire, one will certainly obtain gains;
when clothing is stained with oil, wealth and property will be lost.
When there is an earthquake, external regions will invade.
On the day of the *bhava-aṅga* (the link of existence), if the feet twitch, one hears news of an approaching thief;
if a dog barks at an improper time, the land will not be at peace.
If a crow caws, one will certainly obtain wealth;
when a garment is damaged by a rat, a domestic thief will surely arrive;
when a garment is damaged by fire, one will obtain fine food and drink.
If oil is found on one's clothing, there will be joy; if the earth trembles, there will be abundance and prosperity.
If the feet twitch during the day of one’s birth, one will quickly arrive by means of a distant vehicle;
if a dog barks at an unusual time, it portends a matter of delight.
When the crow caws, there will be peace and harmony without cause for concern;
when the rat damages clothing, one will acquire abundant wealth;
when fire destroys garments, household utensils will increase.
When one's robes are stained with oil, joy will surely come;
if the earth trembles, an army will arrive.
On the day of the "old age and death" branch, when the feet twitch, matters of dispute will prove false.
When a dog barks at an improper time, a friend arrives from afar;
when a crow caws at a specific hour, there will be matters of dispute and litigation;
when a mouse gnaws through clothing, wealth and goods shall be lost.
When clothing is burned by fire, there will be the hardship of imprisonment;
when clothing is stained by oil, matters of dispute will arise;
when an earthquake occurs, the danger lies in the east.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the great assembly:
"If there is anyone who contemplates these twelve links of dependent origination without forgetting them, they will certainly be able to understand matters such as distant sorrows and joys."
If it is the day of the *avidyā* (ignorance) link, one should protect one's wealth and property.
On the day of the *saṃskāra* (volitional formations) link, one should collect or discard wealth and property.
On the day of the *vijñāna* (consciousness) link, one should study arts and skills.
"On the day of the *nāmarūpa* factor, it is auspicious for matters concerning one's retinue.
On the day of the *ṣaḍāyatana* factor, it is auspicious for matters concerning the formation of acquaintances.
If it is the day of the *sparśa* factor, it is appropriate for breaking up enmity."
"On the day of the Vedha branch, matters of marriage are auspicious.
On the day of the Nāga branch, one should carry out royal commands and refrain from unlawful acts.
On the day of the Kula branch, one should attend to affairs of high importance."
"On the day of the link of old age and death, one should not engage in unrighteous deeds or undertake formal practices.
At that time, the great assembly addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"Regarding these twelve links, how should they be applied when performing divinations?"
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly, saying:

"Furthermore, if there is a person who seeks divination on the day of the Ignorance limb (*avidyā-aṅga*), it is auspicious for obtaining wealth and for acquiring saddles and horses; however, it is not to be used for the permanent gathering of kinsmen."
"On the day of the *saṃskāra* lunar mansion, it is auspicious for inquiries, setting out on journeys, eating and drinking, thinking of one's children, minding friends, and preaching the Dharma.

On the day of the *vijñāna* lunar mansion, when making inquiries, one should not move with excessive joy; it is auspicious for forming acquaintances and friendships, for not giving rise to afflictions, for the successful accomplishment of undertakings, and for the cessation of calamities."
"On the day of the *nāmarūpa* link, if one performs divination, there will be fear and affliction, affairs will be dispersed and widespread, and there will be separation from kinsmen.
On the day of the *ṣaḍāyatana* link, when performing divination, one obtains wealth, honors, and services, as well as the pleasure of a wife and the high status of sons and daughters."
"On the day of the contact (*sparśa*) factor, if one seeks counsel regarding disputes, there will be fear of thieves, distress, unjust calamities, and discord among kinsmen.

On the day of the sensation (*vedanā*) factor, if one seeks counsel on matters, one will obtain much wealth and treasure, food, drink, clothing, and bedding, as well as a pleasing wife and be fully provided with ornaments."
"If one seeks divination on the day of the *tṛṣṇā* link, matters conceived by the mind and sought through falsehood will not succeed.
If one seeks divination on the day of the *upādāna* link, those who see [the matter] will rejoice, praise, and protect it; one will obtain seats, vehicles, and wealth, gaining much joy."
"If one seeks counsel on a day governed by the *bhava* link, one will encounter fear of the royal law, destruction, distress, and the separation from kinsmen.

"If one seeks counsel on a day governed by the *jāti* link, one will obtain great wealth, all things will be harmonious, there will be perfect accomplishment, friends will rejoice, and one will be held in high esteem and praised."

Regarding the link of old age and death, one seeks divinations and inquiries; there is false good and evil, destruction and dispersal, a lack of essence, empty matters and great anxiety, and greed and hatred arise frequently.
At that time, having spoken this Dharma, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly:

"If there is anyone who minutely observes the twelvefold dependent origination and thoroughly understands good and evil, sorrow and joy, gain and loss, they should paint a wheel of existence with clear detail.

That is to say, from ignorance down to old age and death, the divisions of months and days should be arranged in succession; the twelve signs—the rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, sheep, monkey, rooster, dog, and pig—with their original forms revolving in sequence, should be explained in order for others."
At that time, the great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, leaped for joy and, with faith and acceptance, practiced accordingly.
*The Sutra on the Auspicious Signs of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, Scroll II.
